sections.title: Connect an agent
sections.text: A workspace owner or admin creates a key on Control → API keys with governance:read and governance:request . Add https://visionxixlabs.com/api/v1/mcp to the agent as a remote MCP server with the header Authorization: Bearer vxlk_live_… . The agent then sees four tools: axiom_check_policy , axiom_request_approval , axiom_get_approval and axiom_record_outcome . The same operations exist as REST endpoints under /api/v1/governance and in the SDKs.

sections.title: How requests are decided
sections.text: Allowed Low-risk work such as reading code, editing a branch or opening a pull request in development or staging. Needs approval Merges, dependency changes, infrastructure, deploys, data migrations, commands and anything in production or an unknown environment. A change whose files touch migrations, CI, auth, infrastructure or secrets also needs approval. Denied Reading production secrets and deleting production resources. These are never approvable through the gateway.

sections.title: Approve or reject
sections.text: Pending requests appear on Control → Agent gateway , with optional webhook alerts ( agent_gateway.request_pending ). An owner or admin who did not create the agent's key decides. Approval covers the exact action and file list, and expires after 24 hours. The agent proceeds only when mayProceed is true, then reports succeeded , failed or abandoned . Each agent gets a scorecard; its trust level is evidence only and never changes what policy allows.

sections.title: Gate a CI deploy
sections.text: Without MCP, use the CLI: vxl ask deploy --target owner/repo --env production --summary "Ship v2" --wait 1800 && ./deploy.sh . It exits 0 only when the action is allowed or approved.

sections.title: Create a key
sections.text: Name the key, choose its permissions and choose when it expires (7 to 90 days). Available permissions: request approvals and report outcomes, check policy and read approval status, read pipeline runs, read the release gate, read webhook endpoints. Wildcard, trigger and admin permissions are not available here. The full key is shown once. V19 stores only a hash and a short prefix, so it cannot show the key again.

sections.title: Separation of duties
sections.text: The person who creates a key is recorded and cannot approve agent gateway requests made with that key. Another owner or admin must decide them.

sections.title: Revoke a key
sections.text: Revoke a key from the list as soon as it may have been exposed or is no longer needed. Revocation takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log. A workspace can hold up to 20 active keys.

sections.title: Risk classification
sections.text: Low risk: read-only checks can execute inline and are still recorded. Medium risk: reversible configuration or repository changes require approval. High risk: deployments and sensitive configuration require approval. Production context: risk can only escalate; it is never reduced for convenience.

sections.title: Approve or reject
sections.text: The proposal shows the requested tool, arguments, risk, workspace, and status. Approval and rejection use separate authenticated endpoints. The Agent cannot approve its own request.

sections.title: Execution requirements and View release review in desktop Deployments
sections.text: In desktop versions with this Overview, open Deployments and select the exact submitted release version. Below Readiness , the Execution requirements panel explains that exact approvals and verified evidence are required before execution. When View release review is available, it opens the merge review for that same release version. Find the button below the scrolling evidence in the wide inspector, or in the toolbar beneath the section tabs in a compact window. Use Tab to reach the button after the section tabs. Opening review records no approval and runs no operation. If View release review is unavailable while the release is refreshing or its version cannot be verified, wait for the refresh or use Refresh before opening review. A draft, closed release or release with no pull request required does not offer this merge review shortcut. A recorded readiness decision of Ready for human review means a reviewer can inspect the request. It does not establish approval, execution or application health.

sections.title: Execution and recovery
sections.text: In the separate-execution preview, approval records review only. The original requester must use a separate execution step for a supported action; current authorization, exact proposal and target checks still apply. An AWS ECS request depends on a separately configured tenant-owned workflow. Approval or dispatch acceptance does not verify ECS execution, service health or rollback; each requires independent outcome evidence. The website preview grants no execution authority.

sections.title: Audit evidence
sections.text: Every tool call receives an action record, including low-risk reads. The record distinguishes proposed, approved, rejected, executed, and failed states so observation is as reviewable as mutation.

sections.title: Answers from the docs
sections.text: Answers come from the public FAQ, documentation and reviewed product facts, and always list their sources. No AI model is used for these answers. When Ask V19 is not confident, it shows the closest guides and offers to open a support request for you to review. Follow a source link to open the guide or page. The chat closes and keyboard focus moves to the cited section or to the page heading. Open Ask V19 again to return to the conversation. Try a plain question such as How do I set up GCP? or How do I block a GitHub Actions deploy until someone approves? The GCP answer explains preview availability; it does not enable a live connection. CI guidance explains a cooperative workflow check, not an approval, deployment or change to GitHub or AWS permissions.

sections.title: Fuller AI answers
sections.text: Signed-in members of a workspace with AI turned on can choose Get a fuller AI answer . It uses prepaid AI credits and the same governed AI path as the Agent. The model sees only the retrieved public passages and must cite them; otherwise the docs answer is kept.

sections.title: Help with your workspace
sections.text: When you are signed in, Ask V19 can tell you what is waiting for approval, which agent requests are pending, which connections are active, when the audit log was last sealed and what happened recently. Every answer is read-only and comes from your current workspace only. Say something is broken or run a health check for a saved-state diagnostic with links to fix each finding. It does not test providers live.

sections.title: What it can do for you
sections.text: Choose Review a support request to carry the question to the contact form in the same tab. Review and edit it before you send. The question stays out of the page address, and opening the form does not submit a request. Ask V19 can also record an access request for a workspace admin to review in Members. Keep the reference to help an admin locate the request. Roles and approvals remain separate decisions. It can also run three fixed actions, governed like any other agent: seal the audit log (owners and admins), verify the audit log (any member) and list API keys expiring soon (owners and admins; it shows names, prefixes and dates, never secrets). Each shows exactly what it will do and runs only after you confirm that action. The server checks your role again, and every run is recorded in the audit log under your name. Sealing adds a record and never edits or deletes events; the other two are read-only.

sections.title: View the audit log from desktop Settings
sections.text: In desktop versions with this shortcut, open Settings → View audit log . V19 opens the website’s Audit & Security page for the workspace selected in the browser. A current workspace owner or administrator can review organization audit evidence. Check the browser workspace before reviewing records. Desktop and browser sign-in are separate. If the shortcut is unavailable in your installed version, sign in to the website and open the Audit & Security directly. If the browser fails to open from Settings, retry from the same button or use the website.

sections.title: Review the original record
sections.text: Open the saved request or task using the history and details controls available in that workflow. Keep its original identifier and version. Compare the displayed source, target, proposed change, actor, review decision and timestamps where those fields are available. Saved metadata is bounded product evidence, not complete provider history. A familiar target name, screenshot or status label alone cannot establish which exact change occurred. Understand execution plans before interpreting their records.

sections.title: Separate decisions from effects
sections.text: Review evidence Who reviewed which exact saved proposal. Approval is not proof that execution was attempted or succeeded. Attempt evidence Whether the supported path recorded a claim or submission and its known result. A completed HTTP request is not by itself an external outcome. Outcome evidence The actual provider observation or readback, its target and observation time. A deployment dispatch does not prove rollback, service health or later availability. Record which evidence is missing. An audit entry is not an independent attestation that an organization is compliant. Hash or export utilities, where available, do not establish complete coverage or independent verification.

sections.title: Handle an uncertain result
sections.text: A timeout does not prove that nothing happened. Do not resend an uncertain or consumed action, edit its history or treat an expired review as current permission. Use supported read-only history or recovery controls first. Keep the difference between refusal before a write, known failure, confirmed result and unknown outcome. Do not infer absence from a blank field or missing response. Recovery is workflow-specific. A readback may establish an external fact without restoring execution authority. Further consequential actions still need the supported current checks and genuine approvals. Troubleshoot an uncertain operation for the next safe inspection step.

sections.title: Share evidence safely
sections.text: Use only the approved support or export path available to your organization. Do not publish tokens, credentials, customer source, private operation identifiers or unredacted screenshots in public URLs or issue comments. Check the target audience and access before sharing. Account help (sign-in required) and the security model and limitations explain adjacent boundaries; neither grants an exception to a consumed attempt.

sections.title: Prepare the repository
sections.text: Add the supported .github/workflows/axiom-deploy-aws-ecs.yml workflow to the repository selected in V19. Limit workflow_dispatch inputs and GitHub environment access to the values your team intends to permit.

sections.title: Create the OIDC trust boundary
sections.text: Create an AWS role whose trust policy accepts the intended GitHub organization, repository, branch or environment. Grant only the ECS and task-definition permissions required by the workflow. Do not use a wildcard repository subject for convenience.

sections.title: Map an V19 environment
sections.text: In the desktop app, create or select an environment and configure its AWS region, ECS cluster, ECS service, and role ARN. The selected environment becomes the deployment target; production context is treated as high risk.

sections.title: Validate before production
sections.text: Run the workflow against a non-production ECS service first. Confirm repository scope, role trust, task-definition capture, steady-state validation, rollback behavior, and the resulting action record before enabling the production target.

sections.title: Desktop source candidate
sections.text: The source candidate adds paired-desktop enrollment for an existing service principal in Settings → Integrations. An accepted workspace owner/admin enters the tenant, subscription, client UUID and secret. The backend verifies the exact tenant/subscription read identity and stores the credential in the canonical tenant-bound encrypted vault. The secret clears after submission and is not persisted in desktop settings. Inventory is an explicit read of at most 100 resource groups from one first page, always labeled incomplete. Validation does not establish Reader-only permissions or VM, storage, security or cost coverage. Disconnect zeroizes V19's stored credential and advances its version; Azure service-principal grants and previously issued tokens are not revoked. Reconnect requires fresh provider validation. This implemented source candidate is not proof of live Azure authorization, production deployment or verified native release availability. Missing storage, configuration or current authority produces an unavailable state. Provider mutation and generic Agent scans remain disabled.

sections.title: What is available
sections.text: Azure credential and configuration-shape validation Runtime mode and credential-presence reporting without exposing secrets Preview snapshots, findings, and recommendations that remain labeled preview An audited scan API that reports whether its source is preview or live Desktop UI states for unavailable, disconnected, and failed connectors

sections.title: What is not verified
sections.text: Live VM, Storage, VNet, NSG, SQL, IAM, or cost inventory Production topology and drift claims derived from live Azure responses Azure action dispatch, retries, validation, or rollback Provider-side evidence proving a real operation occurred

sections.title: Configuration required for a future live path
sections.text: Register an application in the organization's Microsoft Entra tenant. Create a service principal and prefer workload identity federation over a long-lived client secret. Grant only the read permissions needed at subscription or resource-group scope. Enter the Tenant ID, Subscription ID, and Application ID in the installed application. Run a connector test in a dedicated non-production subscription and require an actual ARM response before reporting connected. Download V19 from the release page . Do not create Azure credentials solely for the preview path unless your administrator has supplied an approved evaluation plan.

sections.title: Connect a provider
sections.text: In the desktop app open Batches → Connection . Under More batch providers , enter the API URL and a token. Argo Workflows also needs the one namespace to read. Choose Connect read-only . V19 validates the token with one small read, then stores it encrypted for your workspace. The token is never shown again or sent back to the app.

sections.title: Accepted addresses
sections.text: Prefect Prefect Cloud https://api.prefect.cloud/api/accounts/…/workspaces/… , or a self-hosted https://…/api . Dagster Dagster+ https://your-org.dagster.cloud/deployment , or a self-hosted root. Argo Workflows The Argo Server address (HTTPS) and one namespace. In-cluster and private addresses are refused.

sections.title: What the Agent can read
sections.text: The Automation Agent and the Batches diagnostics skill can list flows, jobs and templates and read recent runs and task runs, up to 20 entries from the first page. Results are observation only and labelled as incomplete coverage. Logs, parameters, artifacts and secrets are never read.

sections.title: Installer availability and download pauses
sections.text: Check Windows availability and the corresponding macOS and Linux links ask the service to check the current release manifest for that platform. If the service confirms an installer, the link can continue to the matching file. Desktop downloads are temporarily paused means the required service storage checks are unavailable. Release status unavailable means the current installer status could not be verified. To recheck installer availability, choose Recheck release status on the download page . From the installer availability screen, choose Return to downloads . Check the release and platform details before installing.

sections.title: What the current desktop build delivers
sections.text: Installed workspace — desktop navigation for releases, approvals, connectors, validation, audit evidence, and related operational views Desktop authentication — browser-approved pairing returns control to the installed application Repository workspace — select, clone, inspect, edit, branch, commit, push, and open pull requests with repository-scoped access Native shell — tray and notification integrations are available for supported application events Explicit connection state — unavailable APIs, missing credentials, and connector failures remain visible Persisted app state — nonsecret preferences use the file-backed app store; session credentials use the configured native vault. Persistence, upgrade migration, and vault-denial recovery require acceptance on each supported operating system.

sections.title: System requirements
sections.text: macOS — Apple Silicon or Intel build matching your Mac; the release currently targets macOS 12 or later Windows — Windows 10 or 11 on x64 with Microsoft Edge WebView2 available Linux — x64 desktop with WebKitGTK 4.1 and GTK 3 runtime dependencies; use AppImage, Debian, or RPM packaging as appropriate Browser engine for Tailwind 4 source builds — Safari 16.4+, Chrome 111+, or Firefox 128+. Desktop webviews need compatible engine updates; the operating-system name alone does not establish compatibility. Qualification on the minimum supported macOS, Windows, and Linux versions remains required before publishing an updated installer. Network — HTTPS access to the configured V19 API and any integrations you enable External accounts — identity-provider and connector accounts remain your organization's responsibility; permissions vary by connector

sections.title: Install — macOS (Apple Silicon + Intel)
sections.text: Visit /download . Choose Apple Silicon or Intel. A verified download link points directly to the matching asset from the current desktop-v* release. Check the download page for the selected installer's verification details. If a matching detached .asc signature and a release public key are published, download both and run gpg --verify installer.dmg.asc installer.dmg using the actual filenames. Compare the SHA-256 digest when one is published. A missing signature or digest means that check is unavailable; if your organization requires it, wait for a release that provides it. Mount the disk image, drag V19 to /Applications , and eject the image. Do not assume the app is signed or notarized. If the download page reports an unsigned developer build, right-click the app, choose Open , and review the warning. Organizations that forbid unsigned software should not install that asset. Choose browser sign-in in the app. Your browser approves the pairing request and the installed application polls for the scoped desktop session. A browser redirect is part of desktop authentication, not a separate web product.

sections.title: Install — Windows x64
sections.text: The generic Windows download prefers the MSI when it is present in the live manifest. The release page also exposes the NSIS .exe . If the selected installer has a matching .asc signature and release public key, verify that signature before running it. Compare the published SHA-256 digest when available. A detached signature does not establish Windows Authenticode signing: use the download page's attestation state and your organization's installation policy. Unsigned builds can trigger SmartScreen. Review the publisher state and your organization's policy before choosing More info → Run anyway . Complete the installer, launch V19, and approve the desktop pairing flow in your browser.

sections.title: Install — Linux x64
sections.text: The generic Linux button prefers AppImage. The release page also provides .deb and .rpm assets when available. When a matching detached .asc signature and release public key are published, verify the selected package before installation. Compare its published SHA-256 digest when available. Do not assume every package includes a signature; if required verification is missing, wait for an appropriate release. Run the commands for the package you verified. These examples use v0.1.25. Substitute the exact filename for the version you downloaded. chmod +x ./V19_0.1.25_amd64.AppImage ./V19_0.1.25_amd64.AppImage sudo dpkg -i ./V19_0.1.25_amd64.deb sudo rpm -i ./V19-0.1.25-1.x86_64.rpm Open V19 from the desktop menu or AppImage and approve the pairing flow in your browser.

sections.title: Desktop installer updates, website deployments and release notes
sections.text: A website deployment does not replace the application installed on your computer. Desktop changes arrive through a separately published installer. In releases that include About this app , open Settings → General and check Installed version . This value comes from the installed app. Unavailable means it could not be read, not that a newer version is installed. Older releases may not have this section. Review releases opens the download page in your browser. It does not download, install, or update the app. Compare the installed version with the selected public release and review that installer's verification details. The current desktop installer does not update automatically. Check the download page for a newer verified tag and install it manually. Review the public V19 release notes before upgrading.

sections.title: Read the proposed change
sections.text: Before reviewing a plan, identify what it proposes and where its effects would occur. Field names vary by workflow; inspect the exact record rather than assuming every plan contains the same fields. Source The repository, branch, tag, commit or other source evidence shown for this request. Check which revision the review actually covers. Target The account, environment, service, ticket or connected-app destination. A familiar name alone is not proof that it is the intended target. Change The exact action and content proposed. Read the displayed payload and limitations before making a decision. Review and window Who must act, the saved revision, and any displayed expiry or execution window. A recorded date is not permission to extend it. Review and execution guidance explains the registered Agent workflow. Release readiness explains why a recorded request is not enough to establish readiness.

sections.title: Keep four different states separate
sections.text: These are concepts for reading a workflow, not a promise that every installed surface uses the same status names or controls. Saved plan The intended work is recorded. Saving does not grant permissions, record an independent decision or prove that a provider was contacted. Independent review An authorized reviewer records a decision about the exact version shown. That decision is not an execution receipt. Who may execute, and whether execution is separate, depends on the supported workflow and installed version. Execution attempt The supported execution path checks current authority and the exact action. An attempt may be refused, fail or remain uncertain. An acknowledgment or completed HTTP request is not proof of the intended external result. Verified outcome Use the workflow’s actual provider observation or readback. A deployment dispatch does not prove application health or rollback; those need their own evidence.

sections.title: When the plan or access changes
sections.text: Compare the current source, target, proposed content and saved revision with the exact review. Do not reuse an expired review or assume an old approval covers changed work. Follow the workflow’s supported refresh or new-review path when it is available. Do not edit old history, extend a deadline yourself or assume a consumed attempt can be renewed. Renewal and recovery rules are workflow-specific; this guide grants no exception.

sections.title: When the outcome is unknown
sections.text: Do not resend an uncertain or consumed action. A timeout does not prove that no write occurred. Keep the original request and inspect its supported read-only history or recovery state. Inspect an uncertain operation before preparing any replacement. If further review is needed, involve the authorized requester and independent reviewer. Do not post private operation identifiers, tokens, source contents or customer data in public URLs. Account help (sign-in required) is separate from reading this public reference.

sections.title: Need a specific answer?
sections.text: See troubleshooting for connection errors, review the plan proposal , or open the in-product documentation from the desktop app.

sections.title: What is available
sections.text: Project ID and service-account JSON shape validation Runtime mode and credential-format reporting without exposing secret values Preview snapshots, findings, and recommendations that remain labeled preview An audited scan API that reports whether its source is preview or live Desktop UI states for unavailable, disconnected, and failed connectors

sections.title: What is not verified
sections.text: Live Compute Engine, Cloud Storage, VPC, firewall, IAM, or billing inventory Production topology and drift claims derived from live GCP responses GCP action dispatch, retries, validation, or rollback Provider-side evidence proving a real operation occurred

sections.title: Configuration required for a future live path
sections.text: Create or select a dedicated non-production Google Cloud project. Create a service account or workload-identity binding with only the required viewer roles. Enable only the APIs needed by the implemented inventory path. Enter the project and approved credential reference in the installed application. Run a connector test and require actual Google Cloud API responses before reporting connected. Download V19 from the release page . Do not provision credentials solely for preview output unless your administrator has supplied an approved evaluation plan.

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.text: A supported macOS, Windows, or Linux system listed on the download page Permission to install software on the workstation HTTPS access to the configured V19 API and any integrations you enable An organization identity and connector accounts supplied by your administrator

sections.title: Step 1 — Download and install
sections.text: Open Download V19 . Choose the architecture that matches your device. When a verified installer is available, its download link opens the matching file. A check availability link asks the service to look up the current release for that platform. Confirm the displayed version and read the platform-specific signing or notarization status. Detached GPG signatures verify release origin, but they do not replace operating-system code signing. Follow your organization's software-installation policy. Follow the desktop installation guide for macOS, Windows, or Linux. If the release is marked unsigned, expect the operating system to warn you; do not bypass that warning where policy forbids unsigned software.

sections.title: Step 2 — Authenticate the desktop
sections.text: The app opens a short-lived pairing flow in your browser. Sign in with the organization identity your administrator configured, review the request, and approve it. V19 polls the pairing status and receives a scoped desktop session after approval. A failed, expired, or rejected request remains visible and must not be reported as connected.

sections.title: Step 3 — Configure integrations
sections.text: A fresh installation should show useful empty states. Add only the repositories, applications, environments, clients, and connectors required for the deployment workflow you intend to run. Begin with the GitHub App and select only the repositories required for your workflow. AWS ECS delivery additionally requires a configured environment target and OIDC role. Other integrations remain unavailable until their server registration and live validation succeed. First check whether desktop enrollment is enabled for that provider and workspace. If the app labels setup blocked, it will not request provider secrets; an administrator must complete the scoped connector-management setup. A successful status must come from a real configured integration response—sample connectors and the website sandbox are never presented as live.

sections.title: Step 4 — Complete a deployment workflow
sections.text: {GOVERNED_JOURNEY.map((stage, index) => ( ))} In desktop builds containing this guide, Documentation provides buttons to open each of these screens. Missing credentials, policy approval or provider validation remain blockers. Capture deployment intake and required operational context. Resolve readiness checks, missing permissions, and dependencies. Generate or select the versioned playbook. Collect required approvals and separation-of-duties decisions. Follow guided execution; unavailable or failed adapters remain explicit. Run validation or schedule deferred validation with an owner. Collect evidence, review audit history, and close only when exit criteria pass. For the released AWS ECS path, approval dispatches the tenant-owned GitHub Actions workflow. Treat any unavailable adapter as a blocker rather than a synthetic success.

sections.title: Example plan metadata
sections.text: This illustrative release intake excerpt records an application, environment, source branch, pending pull request approval, and rollback availability. A complete release request also needs its scoped inputs and evidence. Review all required approvals before execution.

sections.title: Next steps
sections.text: → Desktop installation details → AWS setup and permissions → Explore the isolated product sandbox

sections.title: Who can decide
sections.text: Owners, admins, operators and security reviewers can record an approval. Nobody can approve their own proposal: another authorized reviewer must. The person who proposed an action can always cancel it.

sections.title: Review an action
sections.text: Each pending action shows its tool, risk level and when it was created. Branch, file-commit and pull-request proposals include their exact changes, for example Review file changes or Review pull request . Read them before deciding. For reviewed branch, file, pull-request and AWS restart proposals, approving records your decision only. The requester runs the action separately, and the page says so.

sections.title: Approval rules
sections.text: An approval is bound to the exact action, expires after 24 hours and is used once before the action runs. An expired proposal, or one without an integrity binding, cannot be approved: ask for a fresh proposal, because an old approval cannot restore it. Reject means nothing was executed.

sections.title: What this page shows
sections.text: The inbox shows up to 20 pending actions. It is not a complete approval or outcome history; use the audit log for that.

sections.title: Workspace and platform approvals are different
sections.text: This inbox is for your workspace's Agent proposals. Release, ticket and connected-app reviews belong to their own exact workflows; a decision in one does not authorize an action in another. A workspace owner or reviewer is not automatically an V19 platform administrator. V19's own deployment and issuer controls require separate platform authority. The prepared platform-control workflow remains local development work, not a control available from this inbox or proof of complete Governance enforcement.

sections.title: Read the result before trying again
sections.text: Approval means a decision was recorded; it does not prove an action ran or succeeded. When execution is separate, the original requester must use the exact approved action and the service checks current permissions again. If the result is unknown or a response is lost, retain the original action or request reference and inspect its saved history. Do not automatically resend it, create a replacement, or assume that an expired review means nothing happened. A later observation can add evidence without erasing the original attempt. A provider accepting a command is not proof a deployment is healthy. A recorded issuer drain is not proof existing credentials were revoked or expired. Read the exact workflow's outcome and limitations; a historical record does not grant new permission.

sections.title: Keep policy rules in Git
sections.text: Owners and admins can choose Download policy file under Policy as code on the Governance page. The file lists this workspace's policy rules in a stable, sorted JSON format, so it can be reviewed and versioned like code. Paste a changed file and choose Preview changes to see added, changed and removed rules. Changes that weaken governance are listed under Loosens governance : a rule that no longer blocks releases, is disabled, newly allows exceptions, no longer requires evidence, or is removed. A preview never changes a rule; applying a policy change stays a separate, reviewed action.

sections.title: Promotion lifecycles
sections.text: Under Promotion lifecycles , Governance shows for each repository the order releases move through environments. The order comes from enabled branch policies that require promotion from an earlier environment; environments in the same box have no order between them. Warnings point out gaps: a production environment that can receive a release never deployed to an earlier environment, promotion from the same or a later stage, promotion from an environment that no longer exists, and environments that require promotion from each other. Deployment checks enforce the policies; this view does not change them.

sections.title: Before connecting a provider
sections.text: Set the production V19 origin as NEXTAUTH_URL ; callback construction fails closed when the origin is not trusted. Register the exact HTTPS callback shown below. Wildcard callback domains are not supported. Store client secrets only in the hosting platform's encrypted secret manager—never in NEXT_PUBLIC_* , the desktop app, logs, or Git. Redeploy the service after adding credentials, then use Apps & skills or Settings → Integrations to start consent. Run the harmless validation step. V19 does not label a connection active from consent alone.

sections.title: GitHub App
sections.text: Use this setup to grant the app access to selected repositories. GitHub account sign-in uses a separate OAuth flow. {`$ /api/integrations/github/install-callback`} Set the App slug, App ID, installation-token signing key, and webhook secret using the deployment secret manager. Grant only the repository permissions required by the enabled V19 workflows. A workspace admin reviews GitHub's installation screen and selects repositories. V19 records the installation, then verifies scoped read access before showing it as validated.

sections.title: GitLab repository connection and account sign-in
sections.text: Read-only GitLab repository setup is available only where the workspace feature is enabled. If you see Manage GitLab in Control → Integrations , open it as a workspace owner or admin and select a tracked GitLab repository. If the option is absent, setup is unavailable in that workspace. Use Register project credential to save the exact project ID, expiry date and approved read-only project credential. Pending registration alone does not enable sync. Use Verify read access with the separate verifier in the setup form. Keep tokens out of chat and support requests. Once the status is Read access validated , the bound repository can sync merge requests, releases and existing pipeline evidence. The connection cannot run GitLab CI or modify a repository. If setup is bound to another repository, select that repository to manage the existing binding. Revoke in V19 removes the stored credential and stops V19 sync for that project. Manage the original token separately in GitLab. GitLab account sign-in and linking are separate from repository consent. If your sign-in page offers GitLab, using it identifies your account. It does not connect repositories, grant GitLab CI access or authorize actions in a workspace.

sections.title: GitLab setup status and recovery
sections.text: If GitLab setup says V19 could not confirm the update , first check the current connection for the same repository. Use Refresh status when the connection panel is visible, or Refresh GitLab status if the setup status is unavailable. After saving, Awaiting validation means you can validate the pending project credential. Read access validated means the current repository binding has a valid read check. Revoked in V19 means V19 stopped using the stored credential. A refresh reads the current status without resending your update. If the status remains unavailable, wait for a fresh result before deciding whether to retry.

sections.title: Apache Airflow
sections.text: In the desktop app, a workspace administrator opens Batches → Connection and uses the secure Airflow connection form. Use the HTTPS base address of your Airflow 3 deployment and choose username and password or an existing bearer token. Enter credentials only in the connection form. Select Validate & connect and wait for V19 to confirm the connection. Choose a DAG to inspect available runs. If validation fails or status is unavailable, check the endpoint and credentials and refresh before relying on the evidence. A validated connection gives no automatic permission to start, retry or schedule a run. For Prefect, Dagster and Argo Workflows, see the read-only batch provider guide .

sections.title: Slack
sections.text: Implementation review. Customer OAuth and message delivery are not release-verified. The settings below describe operator configuration. {`$ /api/integrations/slack/callback`} SLACK_CLIENT_ID= SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET= The current workflow requests channels:read and chat:write . It does not request direct messages, private-channel history, commands, or broad message history.

sections.title: Microsoft tenant / Teams
sections.text: The current scope verifies tenant identity. Check your installed version and workspace state before starting consent. {`$ /api/integrations/teams/callback`} MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID= MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET= MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID= The authorization-code flow uses PKCE and currently requests openid , offline_access , and User.Read . This verifies tenant identity; it does not grant Teams messaging authority.

sections.title: Linear
sections.text: Planned. There is no verified customer activation path. The settings below describe operator configuration. {`$ /api/integrations/linear/callback`} LINEAR_CLIENT_ID= LINEAR_CLIENT_SECRET= Consent requests read and issues:create . Mutating Agent actions remain separately approval-gated and auditable after the connection is active.

sections.title: Understand connection states
sections.text: Setup required: the service is missing an OAuth registration, trusted callback origin, or production secret. A workspace user cannot fix this in the desktop app. Awaiting validation: provider consent returned successfully, but V19 has not yet completed a live server-side check. Active / validated read-only: the scoped provider token or GitHub installation passed live validation. Needs attention / validation overdue: validation failed or is stale. Revalidate before relying on the connection for release evidence. Never paste a client secret into Agent chat or a repository file. If a secret was exposed, revoke it at the provider, rotate it in the secret manager, and review the V19 audit trail before reconnecting.

sections.title: Prepare Microsoft Learn documentation search
sections.text: An owner or admin opens Apps & skills → Developer tools (MCP) , chooses Microsoft Learn and confirms Install or Enable . Open MCP tools . Current membership and workspace access are required for requests; the saved installation must be enabled for search. Choose Check connection to see whether the fixed public server responds and offers documentation search. This checks availability only: it does not install the tool, grant cloud access or authorize Agent tools.

sections.title: Search with a public technical topic
sections.text: Enter a short topic, such as Azure App Service managed identity , then choose Search docs . Your topic is sent to Microsoft's public documentation server. Use public terms only; do not paste credentials, private code, personal information or internal incident details. Queries are limited to 300 characters; unsupported or secret-like input is refused. Results show titles, excerpts and links on learn.microsoft.com. They are external reference material, not evidence that your own deployment is configured correctly. V19 bounds request duration and response size, refuses redirects and rate-limits requests. This page lets V19 read a reviewed external documentation tool. To let an external agent request V19 governance decisions, use the separate Agent gateway guide . Neither connection grants the other's permissions.

sections.title: If a request is unavailable
sections.text: Check the workspace's installation state first. Unknown storage state is not an enabled connection. A rate-limit message means wait before trying again. A failed or unconfirmed request is not proof that documentation was read; V19 requires an audit record before confirming it. Do not repeatedly resend sensitive or unsupported input.

sections.title: Roles
sections.text: Owner : full control, one per workspace; ownership moves only through an explicit handoff. Admin : manages members, billing, integrations and every engineer setting. Operator : runs scans, approves engineer actions and configures the workforce, but cannot manage billing or members. Security reviewer : reads findings, approvals and the audit trail, and can vote on approvals but not start engineer actions. Finance viewer : reads cost recommendations and panels, with no write access. Read-only : reads dashboards; no vote, run or manage.

sections.title: Invite a teammate
sections.text: Enter an email address, choose a role (Operator by default) and choose Create invitation link . V19 does not email the link: copy it and send it yourself. The owner role cannot be given by invitation. Starting in the paired app? See workspace access in desktop Settings for the account and workspace checks on the browser shortcut. Invitation links expire after 7 days. Removing a member also voids every earlier invitation for that email.

sections.title: Change a role or remove someone
sections.text: Use Update or Remove on a member's row. You cannot change your own role or the owner's. If V19 cannot confirm the audit record for a change, it says so; check the member list before trying again, because the change may already have happened. If your workspace is enrolled in Governance, promotions and new invitations wait until membership changes have reviewed Governance coverage. Demoting and removing members always work, so you can reduce access at any time.

sections.title: Access requests
sections.text: Members can ask for a higher role through Ask V19. Owners and admins see requests from the last 30 days under Access requests , with the reason given. A request never changes anything by itself: if you agree, change the role in the member list.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Create an OAuth application with the provider (Google Cloud Console / GitHub OAuth Apps). Register the callback URL pointing at your V19 host. Set the resulting Client ID + Client Secret on your host as environment variables. The sign-in page checks /api/auth/providers on load. A provider appears only when that response includes it. The appearance of a sign-in option confirms registration. Verify that the callback succeeds with a test account.

sections.title: 1. Base NextAuth env
sections.text: # Required for every deployment NEXTAUTH_URL=https://your-domain.example.com NEXTAUTH_SECRET= NEXTAUTH_URL must exactly match the public origin (no trailing slash). On Vercel set it under Project → Settings → Environment Variables for Production + Preview environments.

sections.title: 2. Google sign-in
sections.text: Open the Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials . Click Create Credentials → OAuth client ID → Web application . Under Authorized redirect URIs , add: https://your-domain.example.com/api/auth/callback/google For local development add http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google as well. Google shows a Client ID + Client Secret. Treat the secret as you would an API key. GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=1234567890-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=GOCSPX-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx Google's OAuth consent screen needs at least one scope ( openid email profile is the NextAuth default). For external apps you'll need to publish the consent screen to leave test mode and accept non-test users.

sections.title: 3. GitHub sign-in
sections.text: Open GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps and click New OAuth App . Homepage URL: https://your-domain.example.com Authorization callback URL: https://your-domain.example.com/api/auth/callback/github After saving, click Generate a new client secret . GitHub shows the secret once — copy it immediately. GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=Iv1.xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx For an organization-restricted app, create the OAuth app under the org's settings and enable the SSO requirement so only org members can sign in.

sections.title: 4. Verify it works
sections.text: Redeploy after setting the env vars (env changes don't auto-rebuild on most hosts). Open the sign-in page in an incognito window. Confirm the configured options appear. GitHub appears below email sign-in. Complete the provider flow and confirm that the browser returns to V19 Control or the page that requested sign-in. To connect the installed app, complete desktop pairing and approve the requested connection. If you see error=Configuration after the OAuth round-trip, check the host configuration, provider credentials, and registered callback URL.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.text: A provider option is missing Check whether the host has both credentials for that provider, then verify that the provider appears in the sign-in page's provider response. Redirect URI mismatch The exact callback URL registered with the provider must match the one NextAuth requests. For a preview deployment, configure that exact callback URL with the provider or restrict OAuth sign-in to your configured production origin. Works locally but not in production NEXTAUTH_URL not set or doesn't match the production origin. NextAuth uses this to construct callback URLs.

sections.title: Offline AI operations and cloud fallback
sections.text: The v1 model path supports structured Agent decisions through the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions APIs of vLLM, Ollama and LM Studio. V19 does not bundle, install or run a model server. Native server-specific APIs are outside v1. Agent decisions: locally implemented with current membership and policy checks, token reservation, one dispatch and recorded outcomes. Real server acceptance is still required. Bot AI, generic cloud text/coding calls and image generation: unavailable offline in this v1 path. Older local adapters cannot bypass token admission. Cloud fallback and Gateway discovery: refused offline. Online installations cannot select customer-hosted models. Tools and deployments: retain their own connections, permissions and approval gates. The offline AI setting does not make external tools local or certify that the entire application has no external network traffic.

sections.title: Offline customer-hosted models and operator token budgets
sections.text: The deployment operator sets each workspace's token cap and explicit start/end window. There is no automatic token allowance; a missing, unreadable, expired or not-yet-started budget blocks calls. A workspace role named Operator cannot edit the installation's cap. Before dispatch, V19 reserves the full accepted input limit plus output limit, not a guess based on text bytes. Concurrent requests share the durable workspace ledger. Verified usage settles the reservation. Pending, uncertain and overrun liabilities survive configuration and budget-window changes; changing a window does not erase them. Usage is marked customer_hosted_unpriced , not a zero-dollar Gateway bill. Hardware, model licensing and operation can still cost money. If a server misreports usage or violates its accepted limits, V19 records the failure or larger liability; this is not evidence of an inviolable token cap.

sections.title: What the deployment operator prepares
sections.text: The operator supplies AXIOM_LOCAL_MODEL_CONFIG : installation/revision, exact private server URL and host allowlist, approved model IDs, input/output bounds, input byte bound and explicit per-workspace budget windows. These are installation settings, never model output or workspace form fields. AXIOM_OFFLINE_MODE=true selects offline AI; malformed mode settings refuse instead of silently choosing online. Separate protected acceptance records bind the exact configuration and model to real isolated-test evidence, operator review, enforced input/output limits, verified usage and expiry. A hash or a JSON flag alone does not prove server behavior. Source tests use simulated records; no live eligible record is created automatically. The current protected-file reader has a conservative macOS root-owned, non-writable, no-ACL path profile. Other host profiles are not qualified and refuse. Actual provisioning and filesystem/platform qualification remain separate gates; do not weaken ownership or permissions to make setup pass. Offline sign-in, licensing and enterprise custody are separate on-prem requirements.

sections.title: Choose an accepted local model
sections.text: Once an installation is separately qualified, an authorized workspace owner or admin can use AI & Agents → Configuration → Customer-hosted model . Choose an explicitly listed model, then Save model policy . No model is selected automatically. The server rechecks the current accepted model and Governance policy; an enrolled workspace cannot widen AI reach. Desktop Settings → Models offers the same accepted models. Enabling one local model replaces local selection without adding a cloud fallback. The Agent composer sends the exact selected model preference; a changed workspace policy is rechecked by the server. Endpoint and cap changes stay with the deployment operator. Offline · setup required means no accepted model can currently be offered. Ask the deployment operator to inspect the budget, configuration and acceptance expiry. Disable workspace AI remains available to authorized administrators even if no accepted model is listed.

sections.title: Private transport and data boundaries
sections.text: Prompts and schema text are redacted and byte-bounded before use. Host resolution must produce only allowed private addresses; HTTP is restricted to actual loopback, and HTTPS retains hostname/certificate verification. V19 pins the selected address, checks the actual peer and rechecks current admission before sending prompt bytes. One bounded request has a deadline and cancellation. Redirects, public or mixed DNS answers, unexpected models, tool-call responses, missing usage and oversized or malformed responses refuse. No automatic retry or alternate model is used. Your own model-server logging, retention and infrastructure security still need review.

sections.title: Inspect outcomes before recovery
sections.text: Token transitions and a content-free audit record identify the configured model, usage and outcome. Prompt content is not an accounting field. A response lost after dispatch remains uncertain and retains its allowance; a timeout is not proof that nothing happened. Do not repeatedly resend to clear an unknown result or edit a ledger row. Preserve the original history and have the deployment operator inspect server evidence and current policy. Live recovery, independently required approvals and production changes keep their separate review requirements.

sections.title: Workspace roles
sections.text: Workspace membership establishes the tenant boundary. Each supported action checks its required capability at the server; approval authority is distinct from permission to execute.

sections.title: GitHub repository scope
sections.text: The GitHub App installation determines which repositories are available. For a repository action, the service mints a short-lived token scoped to the selected repository rather than reusing a broad user token.

sections.title: Agent authority
sections.text: The decision loop may execute registered low-risk reads. Medium- and high-risk tools create proposals. In the separate-execution preview, an authorized independent reviewer records the decision, then the original requester uses Execute when the action is supported and current checks pass. An approval record is not evidence that a provider action ran.

sections.title: AWS ECS authority
sections.text: V19 dispatches the tenant workflow; GitHub Actions OIDC assumes the environment's configured AWS role. AWS permissions therefore remain constrained by both the GitHub trust subject and the role policy.

sections.title: Browse the Apps and skills catalog
sections.text: Open Apps & skills . Choose Apps , Skills or Developer tools (MCP) , then search by name, description or listed tools. Select an entry's name to inspect its description, status and tools or scopes. Apps are built-in V19 workflows, grouped by provider. They have no separate installation to remove. Choose Manage access to review the provider in Integrations, then use an available governed workflow to prepare an action.

sections.title: Install, disable or remove a skill
sections.text: Current workspace members can browse. Owners and admins with current workspace access can choose Install , Enable , Disable or Remove on supported optional entries, then confirm the named change. Installed guidance becomes available on the Agent's next message; it does not rewrite earlier conversations. Install adds a new skill. Enable reactivates a disabled skill. If the workspace state changed before confirmation, refresh the catalog and choose the action for the current state. In desktop Agent versions with these review skills, explicitly invoke /repository-code-review , /debugging-investigation or /terraform-review to inspect repository source. These invocations use Inspect mode and offer only the skill’s listed read tools, even if Deep Ops is selected. They require the current workspace tool permissions and the relevant GitHub connection. Terraform review reads source and cannot run plan or apply. Use Deployment history review in the desktop Agent to inspect the latest recorded workflow outcomes for a selected environment. Invoke /deployment-history-review and name the environment. This review can read workspace environments and up to 20 recorded executions. Service health, artifact provenance and rollback evidence require their own checks. Installing a skill never grants credentials, changes tool risk or bypasses action approval. Built-in availability, enabled guidance and permission to execute are separate states.

sections.title: Use AWS EC2 observation in Agent
sections.text: In V19 versions that include this skill, open Apps & skills , find AWS EC2 observation and install or enable it for the workspace. In the desktop Agent, send /aws-ec2-observation with one 12-digit AWS account number. Include the account number in the current request and keep tokens and credentials out of the conversation. The skill runs in Inspect mode. It resolves the selected account against the current workspace connections and reads inventory only if there is one connected, unrevoked match and current tool permissions allow it. If no account is selected or the choice is ambiguous, supply a single account number. If the connection is unavailable, review workspace AWS access in Integrations before trying again. The observation covers one page of at most five EC2 instances in one enrolled region at the recorded time. An empty page does not establish that the account has no instances. Costs, utilization, backups, other regions and other resource types remain unknown. Use separate release evidence to assess deployment readiness, service health or rollback.

sections.title: When installation state is unknown
sections.text: If installation storage is unavailable, V19 labels the state unknown and does not offer management controls. If an update is not confirmed, refresh the catalog and inspect the saved state before retrying: the change may have completed even if its audit or response failed. For Microsoft Learn, choose Open tools and follow the MCP documentation-search guide . Arbitrary packages and server URLs cannot be installed from this catalog.

sections.title: The deployment lifecycle
sections.text: Capture deployment intake, ownership, scope, dependencies, and timing. Run readiness checks and surface missing permissions or evidence. Create or select a versioned playbook with validation and rollback expectations. Collect approval gates and enforce separation of duties. Guide execution through an available adapter or an explicitly manual step. Validate the observed result or assign deferred validation with an owner and deadline. Collect evidence, update audit history, communicate status, and close only when exit criteria pass.

sections.title: What users manage
sections.text: Deployment requests and their version history Repositories, applications, clients, environments, and dependencies Playbooks, approval policies, schedules, retries, and rollback expectations Change records, knowledge-transfer sessions, and extracted evidence Validation results, deferred follow-ups, audit history, reports, and exports Connector configuration and actual availability state

sections.title: Availability rules
sections.text: GitHub and AWS live paths require configured, scoped credentials and safe test accounts. Azure and GCP analysis remain preview until live inventory is implemented and verified. Terraform and CLI artifacts can be reviewed; local Terraform apply remains disabled by the desktop safety contract. Communication actions require configured adapters and must surface delivery failures. Every external operation needs resulting evidence before it is marked successful. Use the download page for the current installer and release status.

sections.title: Deployment checks per stage
sections.text: In the cockpit, Checks lets owners and admins attach checks to each release stage (Plan, Validate, Approve, Deploy, Verify and Recover): smoke tests with an expected status and latency, health checks against a metric threshold, migration dry runs in a named workflow job, custom scripts in your repository, manual checklists, security scans (your scanner, with the most critical and high findings allowed) and supply-chain evidence (an SBOM, SLSA provenance or both, verified by your tool). Each check is blocking or advisory and keeps a version that increases with every edit, so a release can record exactly which checks applied. V19 never runs a check. Under CI workflow for these checks , the page generates a GitHub Actions workflow ( .github/workflows/v19-deployment-checks.yml ) that runs the smoke tests and repository scripts for a chosen stage; copy or download it and add it through a pull request. Health checks, migration dry runs and manual checklists are listed with the reason they are not in that file. Each generated job ends by reporting its result to V19 when the repository has a V19_API_KEY secret (an API key with the governance:request scope; it is available to the whole check job, including your scripts) and an optional V19_URL variable. The Checks page then shows each check's last result, and says when it ran an older version of the check. Results are evidence only. Before the desktop app dispatches a deployment, every enabled blocking check at an earlier stage (Plan,

sections.title: Tenants, tags and fan-out
sections.text: In the desktop app, under Settings → Environments, owners and admins can tag each environment with lowercase key:value labels such as tenant:acme , region:eu or ring:1 . Saving uses the same governed configuration path as creating an environment, and an edit is refused if someone changed the tags in the meantime. Tenant fan-out preview takes a selector (all terms must match, and key:* matches any value) and lists the matching environments in ring order, with untagged rings last. It is a plan only: each environment still deploys on its own with its own policy, checks and approvals, and later rings should wait for earlier ones to succeed.

sections.title: Revocation and revalidation
sections.text: Workspace owners can revoke V19's recorded use of a connection from the governed connection record. Provider-side removal remains the source of truth: remove the GitHub App or revoke the OAuth grant in the provider when access must end there too. Validation timestamps distinguish a recorded consent from an active, reachable integration. Do not treat a webhook, browser success screen, or cached status as proof of a live connection.

sections.title: Readiness dimensions
sections.text: {DIMENSIONS.map(([name, detail]) => ( ))}

sections.title: Readiness check states
sections.text: Verified — supported by a current persisted record or actual integration response. Human confirmed — explicitly attested by an authorized user with time and identity recorded. Preview — derived from sample or non-live logic and never treated as production evidence. Unknown — no current evidence; cannot silently pass a gate. Failed or blocked — the check ran and did not satisfy policy, or a required dependency is unavailable.

sections.title: How gates behave
sections.text: Blocking requirements stop progression and identify the owner or dependency needed to continue. Rejected and expired approvals remain recorded and do not count as authorization. Retries preserve prior attempts and their evidence. Closure is unavailable until required evidence and validation are present.

sections.title: What deferred validation records
sections.text: When policy allows deferred validation, record an owner, due time, expected check, and follow-up state. Closure stays unavailable while required validation or evidence is missing.

sections.title: The recovery sequence
sections.text: Resolve and record the task definition currently serving the target. Register or select the requested task definition and update the ECS service. Use ECS's own steady-state waiter as the deployment health boundary. On stabilization failure, restore the captured task definition. Wait for the restored service and preserve the workflow result as evidence.

sections.title: Limits
sections.text: This path restores the ECS task definition. It does not undo database migrations, external side effects, incompatible data changes, or changes made outside the workflow. Teams must keep application-level recovery steps in their own release procedure.

sections.title: Desktop authentication
sections.text: The installed application uses a browser approval handoff and scoped application session. The website is not a customer sign-in product. A packaged PKCE, expiry, logout, replay, recovery, and OS-keychain journey still requires exact-build verification.

sections.title: Connector permissions
sections.text: A connector's code status is not its live availability status. GitHub access is installation- and repository-scoped. AWS ECS deployment requires a configured environment target, tenant workflow, and OIDC role. Azure and GCP production deployment paths are not released. Repository visibility, pull-request approval, merge authority, workflow dispatch, environment approval, release publication, and change management are distinct permissions. Each server-side action must enforce its own authorization.

sections.title: Secret handling
sections.text: Secret-redaction utilities protect supported contact, logging, and operational paths. They do not prove that every field, connector, backup, export, or third-party system is safe for confidential data. Operators must use tenant policy and provider-specific credential guidance.

sections.title: Tenant boundaries
sections.text: Organization identifiers and tenant checks exist across core repositories and services. “Tenant isolated” is not treated as globally verified until every query, cache, background job, export, backup, restore, and administrator path has been exercised against a configured deployment.

sections.title: Audit and evidence
sections.text: Supported workflows can record actor, action, rationale, timestamp, and outcome data. Hash and export utilities exist, but coverage varies by workflow. An audit record is product evidence; it is not an independent auditor's attestation or proof that a customer is compliant.

sections.title: Retention, deletion, and recovery
sections.text: Consistent customer-configurable retention, deletion, backup, and restore behavior is not yet verified across every store. Do not rely on an informal retention period or deletion promise; confirm the configured deployment and record the result in the verification report.

sections.title: Compliance posture
sections.text: No SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, or other independent certification is currently claimed. Control-mapping code is a product feature, not a certification or active audit. No BAA, DPA, data-residency, SSO entitlement, or commercial tier is promised without approved documentation. Customers remain responsible for their own legal, risk, and compliance decisions.

sections.title: Change your display name
sections.text: Open Settings & sessions → Profile . Edit Display name , then choose Save profile . Names must contain 1–80 characters; the server trims surrounding whitespace and normalizes repeated spaces. This changes your own account name, not the workspace name. The profile form cannot change your sign-in email or workspace permissions. If saving is not confirmed, refresh to inspect the saved name before trying again; a failed response does not prove that the change was rolled back.

sections.title: Understand the Security tab
sections.text: Security shows the sign-in email and browser-session status. It is not a password, MFA or role-management form. Use Members and roles for workspace access. Signing out ends the browser session; paired desktop sessions remain independent.

sections.title: Review and revoke a paired device
sections.text: Open Sessions . V19 lists active pairings belonging to your account in the current workspace, with device label, platform, app version when available and last-seen time. It does not show bearer tokens or provider credentials. An unavailable list is not proof that no devices exist. Choose Revoke device , check the named device in the confirmation and confirm. The selected pairing loses access to protected APIs; this does not sign out your browser or revoke other devices. If the result is unconfirmed, refresh the session list before retrying. This revokes the pairing. It does not uninstall the app, erase local files, revoke an independent provider credential or prove that earlier work was cancelled.

sections.title: Desktop settings have a different scope
sections.text: This guide describes browser account settings. The desktop Agent has its own settings and saved session. Use the desktop installation guide for installation and pairing, and confirm the active account and workspace in the app before acting. For the desktop Settings shortcut and browser workspace scope, see View the audit log from desktop Settings .

sections.title: Find the workspace owner and members in desktop Settings
sections.text: In paired versions that show the owner, open Settings → General and look below the workspace ID and device time zone. The Owner row uses accepted owner records from that workspace. Access & roles previews up to three accepted members. Choose View permissions to open the member and role view. If workspace members are unavailable, use Refresh members . An unavailable read does not establish that the workspace has no owner or members. Check that the app is paired to the intended workspace before relying on the result. Invite member , when available, opens Control → Members in the browser. The desktop rechecks your permission and the browser requires the same account and workspace with a current membership. If the browser asks you to return to desktop Permissions, verify the browser account and workspace, then re-open the shortcut from desktop.

sections.title: Local files on your computer
sections.text: In Repositories, the Local strip identifies the selected checkout and its branch. Open Clone or refresh repositories to inspect the source controls. The Local repositories folder lists the local checkouts V19 can discover there; choose the intended repository before opening a file. The editor can contain unsaved changes. A local selection is not a verified GitHub snapshot, and a saved folder selection is navigation metadata, not permission to access a different repository or execute a command. Check the folder, checkout, branch and changed-file count. Use Refresh after changing the folder. If the expected checkout is missing, inspect the folder rather than assuming the selected remote repository is already cloned. Review an edit before Save. Saving a local file does not commit, push, open a pull request or deploy. A check receipt describes that check's recorded result; changed files can make it stale. Inspect the current file and result before relying on it.

sections.title: Connected GitHub repository
sections.text: Clone source · GitHub selects a repository from the workspace's GitHub App access. Refresh connected repositories updates that catalog. Entering another owner/repository does not grant access to it; the provider and server still decide whether that repository is authorized. Local repositories folder is the destination parent folder for Clone. Clone requests a local checkout; selecting a connected repository does not synchronize an existing checkout automatically. Check the local branch and working tree separately before editing or publishing. A connected installation or a repository name is not proof that the current branch, file bytes, pull request or deployment evidence has been verified. Supported actions perform their own checks. Repository reads and provider changes have separate authority boundaries. If the app reports GitHub access is unavailable, Existing local files remain usable. Open Settings → Integrations to review the recorded connection and supported validation controls before cloning or syncing. See integration setup and the permissions model .

sections.title: Preparing context is not sending it
sections.text: Ask Agent prepares an explicitly confirmed selection as an unsent Agent draft. Preparing that draft does not save a file, run a check or send code to a model. Choosing Send later shares the prompt with the approved provider; review it for credentials and private data first. The local selection control limits excerpts and refuses recognized sensitive paths. These controls do not guarantee that an otherwise permitted excerpt contains no secrets. Confirm what is in the draft, which provider is selected and whether sending is enabled for the workspace. AI context does not approve a repository change.

sections.title: Preview, live and recorded evidence
sections.text: Preview can be illustrative data. It is not evidence that a provider action ran. Live or connected describes the data or connection state shown by that view. It does not certify every integration, the current repository revision or deployment success. Recorded results describe an observation at its recorded time and scope. Local files, remote branches and permissions may have changed since then. Do not resend an uncertain or consumed action. Inspect the saved operation and use its supported read-only recovery path. A refresh, old check or previously successful connection cannot supply missing execution evidence. Once the source and intended target are clear, follow the approval workflow . Approval, execution and verified outcome remain separate steps.

sections.title: Choose a desktop destination
sections.text: Open the installed app and use its sidebar. A destination organizes work; it does not authorize a provider action. Read-only inspection, proposing a change, independent review and execution are separate concerns. {DESTINATIONS.map(item=> Next: with synthetic example records. Your workspace shows your own records and the controls your role allows. )}

sections.title: Follow a desktop workflow
sections.text: In desktop versions that include it, open Documentation in the sidebar and select Workflow map . Choose Release, Tickets and recovery, or Batches. Select Fit overview to see the workflow at a glance. Choose a responsibility group to jump to it. Drag an empty part of the canvas to pan when the map extends beyond its viewport. Select a step to open its details and follow a conditional next step . Select Read the guide for the relevant instructions. If the canvas is hard to read at your current window size, use Step list to browse the same steps by group. Use Close details to return focus to the step you opened, or Back to guides to return to the guide reader. The map explains which evidence and approvals a workflow requires. Use the original workspace record to confirm the current version, result and available actions.

sections.title: Follow conditional next steps in the workflow map
sections.text: In desktop versions that include the workflow map, open a step and read the condition below each option in Next steps . Matching a condition is a navigation choice. Use the original release, ticket or batch record to verify which condition applies. On the Release map, Review current authority shows Run the supported operation for Current approval and authority . If approval was rejected or expired, or the saved release changed, choose Hold for review under Rejected, expired or changed . Once the missing evidence or permission is resolved, use Return to review and verify the current saved version. On the Batches map, choose Inspect the run’s tasks for Run failed or task details needed . Follow the failed-run guide from that step for the exact task read. Selecting a branch opens the destination step’s details and moves focus to its heading. Close details returns keyboard focus to the step that opened the details. Read the guide opens the selected step’s documentation. The map is read-only. Use the separate approval and execution workflow for any action.

sections.title: Start, save and resume a release draft from Tickets
sections.text: In desktop versions with Start release draft , open a supported Jira or ServiceNow change in Tickets . Check its reference before opening the draft and review the scope before saving. To pause an unsaved draft, choose Close . During the same signed-in session, return to that ticket and select Resume release draft for followed by its reference. Other tickets keep their own drafts. Choose Save draft , then Open saved release draft to open the exact saved version in Deployments . Choose Return to source ticket to return to the original ticket. If the ticket is unavailable, V19 returns you to ticket search. Saving keeps the draft for review. Submission, approval and execution each have their own controls.

sections.title: Check the collection receipt for incident evidence
sections.text: In desktop versions with Check collection receipt , open the incident in Tickets , choose Evidence and select Review linked release evidence to inspect the linked release. To record collection, an authorized operator needs a completed eligible workflow run and a verified comparison baseline. If Record evidence collection returns an uncertain result, choose Check collection receipt . This read-only check looks up the exact original attempt. If the receipt is still unavailable and Retry evidence collection is offered, that control retries the same collection attempt. A recovered receipt confirms the original collection record only. It does not prove application recovery, successful rollback or current release readiness. Use the incident overview to verify the current release and comparison baseline, and consult the release readiness guide for the remaining checks.

sections.title: Read recorded closure evidence in Deployments
sections.text: In desktop versions with Read closure evidence , use a paired workspace session. Open Deployments and select the exact closed release version. Choose Read closure evidence below Closure recorded . V19 shows the evidence reference and reported outcome saved when that version was closed. If recording the closure returned an uncertain result, resume the closure draft and use Check closure status before attempting another write. If the evidence read is unavailable, confirm the release version and workspace, then try the read again. An unavailable receipt does not tell you that the closure failed. The receipt records a reported external outcome. Use the reference to check the original change or validation record and follow the release readiness guide for independent verification. Reading a receipt does not authorize or dispatch a deployment.

sections.title: Inspect a failed Airflow run in Batches release dependencies
sections.text: In desktop versions with Inspect failed run , open Batches , choose Release dependencies , select the exact submitted release version and select Check batches . The check requires pipeline read access and uses the Airflow runs declared on that version. If a run failed, select Inspect failed run to open the first recorded failed run’s tasks. V19 moves focus to that run’s task control. To choose another observed run, select Inspect tasks below its workflow and run. Waiting or unverified results leave readiness unresolved. The failed-run shortcut only appears after a recorded failure. If the release version changed, reopen the current release and check its declared runs again. In versions with the Observed task states table, read the task’s status, try number, and start and end times in UTC. Missing times show as unavailable. V19 clears the old rows when a task page fails to load. Choose Retry tasks to reread that same page, or Previous task page to return to the previous page when the control is available. Task inspection reads provider evidence. To retry an Airflow run or execute a deployment, use the separately authorized workflow. For a completed check, return to the release approval workflow .

sections.title: Find older closed releases in Batches History
sections.text: In desktop versions with the History action, use a paired workspace session and open Batches → Release dependencies . Choose History beside the Batches heading to load older closed releases with declared Airflow runs. The archive skips closed releases already in the recent list. Use Load more history for the next page, or Retry history if a page could not be verified. Search filters the loaded releases, including pages you opened in this visit. Select the historical row and check the saved version and recorded UTC closing time, when available.
