Choose Open release to view that version in Deployments, then follow the recorded closure evidence guide . Choose Return to Batches to restore the historical row. Batches History shows saved closed release records. A closure receipt records a reported outcome. Use Airflow run evidence and independent validation for provider outcomes and application health. Viewing saved history makes no Airflow request and grants no approval or execution authority.

sections.title: Find release logs in desktop Batches
sections.text: In desktop versions with Open release logs , choose Batches → Release dependencies and select the saved release. Open Logs , then choose Open release logs to open the exact release version’s Logs section in Deployments . In versions with Find recorded workflow logs , choose it to open Evidence . Load the evidence plans, choose the saved plan, and select Read recorded workflow commit . When the saved observation matches the accepted dispatch, choose Open recorded workflow logs to return to Logs. The recorded timeline shows the run and attempt, when the dispatch was accepted, and when the outcome was last observed, in UTC. Use the GitHub link to open that exact attempt. In versions with Review workflow evidence , Logs states why the exact attempt is unavailable, such as a missing run receipt or more than one matching observation. It never implies a deployment outcome. Airflow task logs and live application health are unavailable in this view. Use the failed Airflow run guide to inspect observed task state and try numbers. From Deployments → Logs , use Return to Batches to restore the selected release, open Logs section and keyboard focus. If search has hidden the selection, clear the search to show the same version again. If a refresh finds a newer version, select it explicitly before opening its logs.

sections.title: Open a release record in the browser
sections.text: Some desktop views offer Open release record in browser . The record opens in the cockpit for your active workspace and is read-only. The heading shows the release tag, or Untagged release when none is recorded. Status , Release ID and Commit show the recorded values. Awaiting a recorded commit means no commit is stored yet. Linked change tickets lists up to 50 linked tickets, or says none are recorded. Release actions stay in V19 Studio. If the page says Release unavailable , check the workspace selector and reopen the link from the desktop app.

sections.title: Use the website for guidance
sections.text: Download the desktop app — inspect the current manifest-backed installer and platform-specific verification information. Public documentation — read setup, workflow and recovery references without starting an action. Illustrative demo — explore the explanation of a workflow. Demo content is not a live workspace or evidence that an action ran. Account help (sign-in required) — use the authenticated help surface when available; this public guide grants no account access. Browser sign-in and provider-consent pages support specific authentication or connection steps. Returning from a browser does not by itself prove that desktop pairing, connection validation or an operation succeeded.

sections.title: Watch a V19 desktop recording or scripted tour
sections.text: The public demo is a scripted tour with sample data. An authentic desktop recording is currently unavailable. The tour explains the workflow without running a provider action. When a reviewed recording is available on the homepage, its player shows the exact V19 version, platform and build source, with a still preview, captions and a transcript. Playback starts when you choose Play.

sections.title: Know who acts next
sections.text: The person preparing work checks its exact source, target and content. An authorized independent reviewer makes the required decision personally. Who executes next, and whether execution is a separate control, depends on the supported workflow and installed version. See Review and execution guidance . If a connection or permission is missing, use its supported setup path or ask the authorized administrator. A different screen, a catalogue entry or an old approval does not remove that requirement. Do not resend an uncertain or consumed action. Inspect the original saved record using the supported read-only history or recovery controls. A different destination is not a retry permission. Troubleshoot the current state before preparing another action.

sections.title: Install or sign in
sections.text: Check the selected release and installer on the download page. Choose the package for your operating system and architecture, then follow the installation guide. Desktop sign-in uses browser-approved pairing; return to the installed app to continue. Availability and verification depend on the selected release. This guide does not establish signing, platform acceptance, or a successful clean installation. Follow your organization’s software policy and platform protections. Check downloads · Install and sign in

sections.title: A connection is not ready
sections.text: Start from Connect in the installed app’s Integrations area, not a callback URL. Setup required needs the service operator; awaiting validation means consent alone is incomplete. Revalidate a failed or stale connection before relying on it for evidence, where that control is available in your installed version and surface. Validated read access does not establish authority for every write. Installing the app does not make a connection ready, and workspace users cannot supply missing production registration or secrets in the desktop app. Understand connection states · Operator setup

sections.title: A review is stale, expired, or unavailable
sections.text: Check the current proposal, target, permissions, and installed-version guidance. Approval is a review record; it does not prove execution or success. An expired or changed review cannot be treated as current authority. Use the normal proposal and independent-review process for current details only after checking whether an original operation already exists. Do not reuse expired approval or work around disabled controls, missing authority, baseline restrictions, or unavailable evidence. For the registered Agent proposal workflow described in the approval guide, separate requester execution remains a local preview and is not production-activated. Your installed version may not include an Execute control. Recovery controls depend on the installed version and surface; this article does not enable them or grant execution authority. Approval permission and execution permission remain separate. Approval and execution boundaries · Readiness guidance

sections.title: The original operation is uncertain or consumed
sections.text: Read the original saved operation and available outcome evidence using the controls supported by your installed version. Saved metadata is bounded evidence, not complete provider history. A consumed operation cannot be repeated through a replacement request, and waiting for a lease does not restore permission. Any provider reconciliation must be read-only and authorized; no automatic reconciliation service is implied. If the result remains uncertain, seek help with a sanitized summary. Execution and recovery · Audit evidence guide

sections.title: Get help safely
sections.text: Account help (sign-in required) · Service status · Contact Share your app version, operating system, affected task, approximate time, visible status, and a sanitized error summary. Omit passwords, tokens, client secrets, authorization codes, callback state, tenant secrets, and sensitive repository or customer content. Keep original operation IDs private and share them only through an approved support channel; do not put them in public posts or URLs. Review what you share yourself; this guide does not promise automatic redaction or a response time. Founding Supporters funds development; it is separate from technical support.

sections.title: Seal and verify the audit log
sections.text: Owners and admins seal recent audit events. Each seal fingerprints a window of events and links to the previous seal, forming a chain. Anyone in the workspace can verify: the result is intact, or names the seal whose events changed or whose link broke. Because someone who can rewrite the database could also rebuild the chain, download an anchor after sealing and keep it somewhere V19 cannot write, such as a ticket, a vault or an email to your auditors. The anchor holds the latest seal's fingerprint and no event content. Later, choose Check a kept anchor : V19 reports whether that seal still matches, is missing or was rewritten, and refuses an anchor file that was edited or belongs to another workspace. Sealing does not stop someone from changing data; it makes the change visible. Store the latest seal fingerprint outside V19 so a rewritten chain is also detectable.

sections.title: Replay a draft rule
sections.text: Pick a draft rule and replay it over up to 90 days of real approval history, through the same rule engine production uses. You see how many actions it would newly block or auto-approve, and each changed action. Nothing is enabled or saved. History does not store a finding category, so rules that match on category are skipped and named rather than guessed.

sections.title: Preview a change
sections.text: Paste the changed file paths. The preview lists the areas touched (migrations, CI, auth, infrastructure, dependencies, secrets, API, frontend, tests, docs), the blast radius, whether a rollback plan is needed, and what a reviewer should check. It reads file names only, never contents.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Shows your plan, the AI allowance remaining, seats, counted deployments and gateway calls, plus AI usage for the current UTC month. AI cost is settled from the gateway's generation cost; calls still awaiting settlement are counted as pending, never as free. Credits increase only from payment records verified by Stripe. Buying AI credit top-ups is currently unavailable while one-time payment fulfillment, refunds and replay handling are verified. The page states this; no charge can start while it is off.

sections.title: Usage records
sections.text: Every member can browse AI usage records for the last 12 months, 50 per page, filter by settled or pending, and export the current page. Times are in UTC.

sections.title: Invoices and payment details
sections.text: Owners and admins see invoices and can open the secure Stripe billing portal with Manage billing when billing is enabled for the workspace. Other members see who manages billing instead.

sections.title: Choose an active workspace
sections.text: When more than one workspace is available, use the sidebar's Active workspace selector, choose the intended workspace and select Open workspace . The browser opens Control in that workspace. With one current workspace, the sidebar may show its name without a selector. The server checks your signed-in account and accepted membership before saving the browser selection. Recheck the workspace name and role before preparing any action. Switching does not copy records, create a connection or carry an approval into another workspace.

sections.title: Recover unavailable workspace access
sections.text: Workspaces is a recovery destination that directs you to the sidebar. If the current selection is no longer available, choose another workspace offered to your account and select Open workspace . A pending invitation or workspace identifier alone does not establish accepted membership. If no valid workspace is offered, confirm the signed-in account and ask an owner or admin to review membership. Do not repeatedly submit a removed workspace or treat a cached page as current access. See Members and roles for invitations and access requests.

sections.title: Browser context and paired devices are separate
sections.text: Browser workspace selection does not switch or re-pair the desktop Agent. Check the account and workspace in each surface before continuing. Use Settings and sessions to inspect your paired devices for the current workspace. Every protected operation still needs its own current role, provider access, policy and approval checks. Opening a workspace is not permission to deploy or approve someone else's request.

sections.title: Delivery insights for the workspace
sections.text: In the cockpit, Insights shows how often the workspace ships and how quickly it recovers: workflow runs and runs per week, run success rate and median time to complete over the last 30 days, and open incidents with median time to mitigate and resolve over the last 90 days. Figures come only from recorded workflow runs and incidents. A workflow failure is not always a failed change, and lead time from commit is not measured, so treat these as operating signals rather than DORA certification. When blocking deployment checks exist, Insights also counts how many recorded deployments in the window had passing evidence for every one of them, how many had a failed check, and how many had no evidence (for example runs before a check was added, or emergency bypasses). It uses today's blocking checks and matches results by commit.

sections.title: Configuration variables per environment
sections.text: In the cockpit, Variables holds plain configuration such as a base URL, log level or feature switch. Set a workspace default, then override it for an environment that needs a different value; environments without an override inherit the default. A notice lists names that are set for some environments but have no default, so a missing value is visible before a release. Each environment shows a short fingerprint of what it resolves to, which changes whenever any value it sees changes. Owners and admins can add, edit and remove variables. Edits carry the version you loaded, so a change made by someone else in the meantime is reported instead of overwritten. Names and values that look like credentials are refused: keep secrets in scoped credentials. Passing variables into deployment workflows is not connected yet, so this page does not change any running service. When the desktop app dispatches a deployment to an environment, V19 records that environment's fingerprint and resolved values with the deployment. Each fingerprint card then says whether the configuration still matches the last recorded deployment or has changed since. Feature switches shows every variable named FEATURE_… as on, off or its value in each environment, so staged exposure is visible at a glance. Compare before promoting lists the values that differ between two environments, and names that exist in only one of them. If the snapshot cannot be recorded, the deployment still runs and the card says no fingerprin
